title: Do you think that AI giants will prevent us from owning computers?
author: Limp_Bus3865
selftext:
I just assembled two towers for game development, because my og PC is getting kind of old and creating games has become a bottleneck, especially because my last two games run on my own game engine I recompile a lot.   
We all know that GPU and RAM prices are through the roof and I see no end in sight. Even if the "bubble" bursts, still, AI is developing week by week and soon I think they will need even more different computer components for building robots. Because robots are the bottleneck between AI and manual labor.   
The prices are ridiculous already, but I think they will be even worse. And we cannot develop anything if we don't have a good GPU, CPU and RAM, especially in the age of AI where you can maximize the usage of it, since AI doesn't sleep and coding/testing/recompiling is running more often, because it doesn't wait for you and your team as long as it used to.   
Sony is now fighting against physical media, not just with PS, but also with their other BR reading products. I think the next step in tech is that they will push everything on the cloud, especially because now we can decompile proprietary software.   
What are your thoughts? Any of you stocking up on RAM?

replies.author: cheyumaama
replies.body: That's the way it's headed but the benefit is the lower barrier for entry. To rent a high end Nvidia GPU right now, it's only $1.50-$2/hr. You do your work or model training for hours and then save to your S3 bucket and close the session. You can even train massive 1 trillion+ parameter models this way. Of course, it will still cost a decent amount of money but you don't need to have your own data center, storage servers and all that
